_what_this_is: C0 donor-house material set. Seven roles, ten mesh slots.
_why_seven_not_ten: Four slots (Material_001_ncl_1, _002, _004, _006) all reference the SAME source texture, rough_wood_diff_2k, so all four map to one role. That is consolidation, not a collision -- read from the mesh wiring at _verify/20260830_c0/slot_wiring.json, not assumed.
_measured_vs_authored: albedo is a real file. normal is DERIVED from albedo luminance (an approximation -- see scripts/derive_material_maps.py). roughness_base is AUTHORED: there is no route from a diffuse photograph to a physical roughness, and a number with no ground truth must be labelled as one.
_normal_convention: DX (green down). MEASURED, not assumed: derive_material_maps.py --calibrate labels ambientCG's ten vendor-labelled DX/GL files 10 of 10 correctly, red control +0.53 to +0.90.

unit_scale_check.verdict: 1 uu = 1 cm confirmed; not a metres-scale Blender export

_grade_ruling: +90% saturation and 4.0x warmth measured on the flat stage were ruled real and too far. wall_planks_b and roof_tiles graded toward the MIDPOINT of the two measured endpoints; beam_wood darkened 0.90x toward the concept chalets. Luminance DETAIL deliberately untouched -- that is what makes the timber read against the plaster, and the ruling asked to keep it. scripts/grade_albedo.py; targets and residuals in _verify/20260830_overnight/grade_plan.json.
_tiling_is_derived: TILING IS COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED: tiling = metres_per_uv / tile_m, with metres_per_uv MEASURED per slot by the uv-density pass and tile_m measured above. Until 2026-08-31 the master's `Tiling` scalar sat at its 1.0 default and nothing ever wrote it, so all seven roles rendered at the machine unwrap's own density -- and, worse, at the SAME density as each other despite tile_m spanning 0.5 m (rough_wood) to 8.0 m (grey_roof_01), a 16x relative error between two roles on one house. EVERY C0 JUDGEMENT INCLUDING THE GRADE WAS MADE UNDER THAT.
